description: 🌐 The open-source Agentic browser; alternative to ChatGPT Atlas, Perplexity Comet, Dia.

summary.one_liner: BrowserOS is an open-source Chromium-based agentic browser monorepo that ships two products: BrowserOS neo, a secondary browser that AI agents drive using your logged-in sessions, and BrowserOS, a Chromium fork with a built-in AI agent for human browsing.
summary.what_it_does: BrowserOS neo is a separate browser meant to sit beside Chrome; it imports logins, bookmarks and extensions from Chrome in one click and exposes an MCP endpoint so agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and VS Code can hand it web tasks. Multiple agents run in parallel, each in its own tab, and a live dashboard shows what each is doing. Every session is saved locally as a replayable video with an action timeline under ~/.browserclaw/. The BrowserOS product is a Chromium fork with an AI agent in every new tab, usable with your own AI keys or local Ollama models. The repo contains both the Chromium fork (C++/Python build system, patches) and the agent platform (TypeScript/Bun and Rust crates, WXT/React extensions, Vite onboarding flows).
use_cases: Let AI agents work in my logged-in browser accounts
Automate posting and engagement on LinkedIn or Twitter/X
Clear inbox and unsubscribe from email via an agent
Connect Claude Code or Codex to a real browser
Replay and audit what an AI agent did in a browser session
Run multiple browser agent tasks in parallel
how_to_run: Or download the macOS, Windows, or Linux x64 (AppImage/DEB) build directly
Import logins from Chrome in the onboarding flow
Connect an agent such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor from the app
Developers: see the contributing guides; the browser build needs ~100GB of disk
notable: Uses your real logged-in Chrome profile rather than a blank headless sandbox
Runs locally on 127.0.0.1; sessions, screenshots and history stay on disk
One-click connection to multiple AI coding harnesses via MCP
Session replay as a scrubbable video with step timeline
Two products in one monorepo: neo for agents, BrowserOS for humans
caveats: Building the Chromium browser requires roughly 100GB of disk space
Neo's Linux builds are x64 only
Sends anonymous product-usage telemetry by default (can be turned off in Settings)
README does not state the Linux build status beyond x64 AppImage and DEB
